transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Ethan Park (Redwood) / Dr. Samir Rao, Leah Ortiz, Naveen Gupta (Praxis Health)

Summary: Short discovery to understand Praxis's requirements for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment of Redwood Private for PHI/regulated workloads. Focus on offline updates, hardware, and compliance constraints.

[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Maya, AE, and Ethan is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Dr. Samir Rao (Praxis CTO): Hi, Samir here. Leah and Naveen with me. We run the ML platform and infra at Praxis.
[00:20] Maya: Awesome, do you want to start with a quick context on what you're trying to build and why on-prem/air-gap is critical?
[00:30] Leah Ortiz (Infra): Sure. We're a healthcare tech provider, lots of PHI, regulatory audits. our compliance team will not allow external outbound connections from the inference cluster. so anything that calls home is a no.
[00:45] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): Understood. When you say "no outbound," do you mean no internet egress at all, or a controlled jumpbox with cached artifacts?
[00:54] Leah: Ideally no egress. We do allow controlled jumpbox processes for scheduled updates but it's highly audited, manual approvals, air gap procedures.
[01:05] Maya: Okay, good. can you describe the update cadence you expect for models and runtime patches? monthly, quarterly?
[01:15] Dr. Rao: For models, initial pilot we expect monthly updates. long term maybe quarterly depending on QA. For security patches we need a process to pull packages offline and validate in a staging air-gapped network before injection.
[01:28] Naveen Gupta (Sec Eng): Also need to understand how keys are injected. we use an on-prem HSM and we cannot export keys, so any KMS integration must support key wrap or bring-your-own-key with HSM onboarding.
[01:42] Ethan: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS via HSM integrations and can operate without outbound connectivity if you handle package delivery. we have an "air-gapped update" playbook that describes artifact bundles and signature verification.
[01:55] Leah: Can you describe artifact bundles? we don't want a continuous sync, we want a signed tarball or usb method that we can validate.
[02:06] Ethan: Yes, typically we produce a signed bundle containing model weights (optionally quantized), runtime binaries, and a metadata manifest with checksums and signatures. your infra team verifies signatures using the Redwood signing key or we can sign with a customer key if preferred.
[02:24] Dr. Rao: signing with our key is preferred. we can't rely on external keys.
[02:30] Ethan: That is doable — we have a process for customer-signed manifests. it's a manual step in the pilot but can be automated in your CI if you accept the key exchange.
[02:40] Maya: Great. wanted to cover hardware — what are you planning to provision?
[02:45] Leah: We're evaluating H100s for perf but our procurement cycle might only allow A100s initially. we want to understand the perf delta and whether Redwood can support both.
[02:56] Ethan: Redwood runtime supports both H100 and A100; H100 will be faster and more memory efficient for newer models but we can provide sizing guidance. for air-gapped installs we usually ship a runtime optimized per hardware profile.
[03:10] Naveen: Memory footprint is a concern, our node types are NVRAM-limited. what's the recommendation for model quantization or sharding across GPUs?
[03:20] Ethan: For on-prem, we recommend quantized 4-bit/8-bit variants for cost and memory. we also support tensor-slicing across GPUs for large models, and we can provide a config that maps model partitions to GPU topology.
[03:34] Dr. Rao: how about latency? our product needs sub-200ms p95 for short prompts. can you hit that on A100s?
[03:44] Ethan: Depends on model and prompt length. for smaller LLMs (e.g., 7B-13B quantized) hitting p95 <200ms is achievable with right batching disabled for low-latency mode and prefetched KV cache. with large models you'd need more optimized runtime and H100 is preferred.
[04:05] Leah: What's the process for fallback? say you want to upgrade but QA fails. can we run two versions in parallel?
[04:12] Maya: Yes — Redwood supports pinned model versions and can do canary and A/B rollouts. in private mode you can deploy multiple model variants and route traffic via your AB testing layer; the console supports rollbacks.
[04:25] Naveen: auditability is key. we need immutable logs for inference requests, who updated what models, and when. retention for audit logs at least 2 years.
[04:36] Ethan: We can integrate with your on-prem logging stack (e.g., ELK) and ship structured logs. we also maintain local audit logs and can sign log bundles. retention policies are configurable.
[04:48] Dr. Rao: okay, specific questions on upgrades: we want ability to validate model outputs in a staging air-gapped env then promote. does your packaging support staged promotion without external calls?
[04:59] Ethan: Yes — the bundle contains versioned manifests and metadata. promotion is a local orchestration step: the agent verifies signatures, unpacks, runs a smoke test harness, and then flips the symlink to the new model. no outbound required.
[05:15] Maya: timeline — are you looking to start a pilot soon?
[05:19] Dr. Rao: procurement timeline is tight; hoping to start a pilot in 6-8 weeks, must be on-prem and air-gapped. decision-makers: myself, Leah, and compliance (not on this call).
[05:30] Leah: budget question — can you give a rough cost delta between Dedicated hosted vs Private on-prem?
[05:36] Maya: we'll provide formal pricing. high-level: hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity on Redwood-managed infra; Private includes a base platform fee plus support and optionally a one-time setup for on-prem air-gapped installation. we'll send a comparison.
[05:50] Naveen: about encryption — do you support FIPS modules and HSM-backed keys?
[05:55] Ethan: We support KMS integrations and can accept keys from on-prem HSMs; FIPS mode depends on your distro and kernel, but we can run in FIPS-compliant mode if your environment supports it.
[06:07] Dr. Rao: any compliance docs we can review? SOC 2, ISO, penetration test reports?
[06:12] Maya: yes, we'll share SOC 2 and ISO artifacts and our SOC package under NDA. also the deployment checklist for air-gapped installs.
[06:20] Leah: monitoring — we cannot have telemetry leave the network; we need local dashboards. can Redwood Console run in private?
[06:28] Ethan: Redwood Console can be installed as part of the Private deployment with a local control plane. for hosted dashboards, we can export reports, but for air-gapped customers we ship a console instance that integrates with your local Grafana/Prometheus.
[06:42] Maya: Any blockers we haven't covered?
[06:45] Naveen: licensing/legal — we need to review EULA for on-prem installs and indemnities. also need clarity on support SLAs for on-site incidents.
[06:56] Maya: We'll include support tiers and SLA options in the follow up.
[07:00] Dr. Rao: one technical nit — can Redwood runtime operate without root privileges? our security team forbids daemons as root in production clusters.
[07:08] Ethan: The runtime can run under a dedicated user and non-root container; some GPU drivers require elevated privileges for device access, usually we rely on the cluster admin to configure device plugins. We can provide best practices for non-root deployments.
[07:25] Leah: what's your recommended sizing for 100 qps of short prompts (avg 64 tokens) across 13B model quantized?
[07:34] Ethan: Rough estimate: 3-4 A100s in a pool with concurrency tuning and low-latency configs. we'll provide an exact sizing spreadsheet after seeing real prompt distributions.
[07:48] Maya: We'll send a perf spreadsheet and three sizing options (cost-optimized, latency-optimized, balanced).
[07:55] Naveen: offline attestation — can you provide signed binaries and a reproducible build? our process requires deterministic hashes for binaries.
[08:03] Ethan: We can provide signed builds and a reproducible build artifact manifest. some components are proprietary but we can provide checksums and a reproducible build log for what we ship.
[08:18] Dr. Rao: Any red flags from your side on our constraints?
[08:22] Maya: nothing major; air-gapped installs are standard for enterprise healthcare. timeline and procurement might be the gating items.
[08:30] Leah: Great. how do we proceed on the pilot?
[08:34] Maya: Proposed next steps: send air-gap deployment playbook, pricing options, hardware sizing sheet, and schedule a bench window. can we set target dates?
[08:45] Dr. Rao: yes — we'll aim to confirm procurement and network diagrams by 3/9 so you can schedule benching mid-late March.
[08:55] Maya: Perfect. we'll follow up with the docs and a proposed bench date.
[09:00] Ethan: quick question on fallback strategies: if you can't get H100s what tuning should you plan for?
[09:06] Ethan (cont): (mumbles) on A100s we push quantization and smaller model sizes, maybe a 13B quantized rather than 70B.
[09:15] Leah: understood.
[09:18] Maya: Any final questions?
[09:21] Naveen: nothing more on my end.
[09:23] Dr. Rao: thanks, appreciated.
[09:25] Maya: Thanks everyone. recap of next steps: Maya to send guide and pricing, Ethan to do sizing and perf notes, Praxis to share network diagram. we'll capture action items in the CRM.
[09:40] End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-recognitions present (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash" in internal notes), speaker attribution in some sections may be generic.

Recap (end):
- Action items and owners captured above.
- Pilot target: start in ~6 weeks pending procurement and network readiness.
- Key risks: procurement delay; H100 availability; legal review of on-prem license.

References mentioned: air-gapped deployment playbook (link: redwood.com/airgap-playbook - placeholder), SOC 2 pack (NDA), sizing spreadsheet (to be attached).
